description:
=== DONE (s473t5d) ===
FOUND + FIXED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5.

t/io/inplace.t failed ALL SIX of its rows on

  Can't open /tmp/pcl-test-N-1: No such file or directory

The fixtures are built by

  runperl( prog => 'print qq(foo\n);', args => ['>', $file] );

i.e. the SHELL redirects the child's stdout into the file.  PCL's stub did

  my $argv = join(' ', map { quotemeta($_) } @{$opts{args} // []});

so the `>` became `\>` -- a literal argument -- and the file was never created.

The REAL t/test.pl appends `args` RAW: its `_quote_args` adds double quotes
only on VMS, and `_create_runperl` then does
`$runperl = _quote_args($runperl, $args{args})`.  One line, matching perl.

BLAST RADIUS, measured rather than assumed: nine files in perl's t/ pass
`args =>` to runperl (io/inplace.t io/iprefix.t op/caller.t op/sprintf2.t
run/locale.t run/switchC.t run/switchd.t run/switches.t run/switchx.t) and none
of their values needs quoting (plain words, filenames, `>`, `chr(256)`).  In the
SWEEP population only perl-tests/caller.t passes `args =>` to runperl (its
values are `qw()` words, where quotemeta is the identity) -- perl-tests/
sprintf2.t's `args =>` is its own sprintf data -- so the sweep cannot move from
this change, and it did not.

RESULT: t/io/inplace.t 2/6 -> 6/2 (4 blessed rows left the baseline by EDIT).
The residue is 2 rows (`die shouldn't touch file`, `last should update file`) --
the in-place edit's behaviour on an ABNORMAL exit; #1710 carries them.
Guard tools/t/harness-switches.t rows 3+4.
subject: perl-tests/t/test.pl's run_perl() quotemeta'd `args`, where the real t/test.pl appends them RAW -- so `args => [">", $file]` became a literal argument instead of a shell redirect and the fixtures were never written
